subject: maths
question: A train 200 meters long is traveling at a speed of 72 km/h. How long will it take to pass a platform 100 meters long?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total **Distance** = 200 + 100 = 300 m

**Speed** in m/s = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s

**Time** = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 15 seconds.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **train** (L₁) = 200 m

Length of the **platform** (L₂) = 100 m

**Speed** of the train (S) = 72 km/h

**Formula Used:**

**Time** = (Length of train + Length of platform) ÷ **Speed**

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aadfde23c40ad306a8c1655c0072267006452be8dd9b3d5232a1a9ee96bcab1f.png] 

⇒ Total **Distance** to be covered = 200 + 100 = 300 m

⇒ **Speed** in m/s = 72 × (5 ÷ 18)

⇒ **Speed** = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

⇒ **Time** taken = 300 ÷ 20

⇒ **Time** taken = 15 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 15 seconds.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **opposite direction**, their relative speed is the **sum** of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Train passing a Point Object

When a train passes a **pole**, a **tree**, or a **stationary man**, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train** itself.</p
